# Data source

A data source read through the Connectors command line: the configured source (a Connectors adapter alias, a connection and the read operation it declares for each kind of read), how the command line is run, what `operations describe` reports for an operation and what one read answers. A read never carries a credential and never runs an operation Connectors describes as a mutation.

`loom.datasource` is one of loom's bounded contexts. [All domains](./index.mdx).

## Types

### `AdapterAlias`

`loom.datasource.AdapterAlias` wraps `String` and is not interchangeable with one: the whole value of naming it separately is the crossings the model then refuses.

### `ConnectionId`

`loom.datasource.ConnectionId` wraps `String` and is not interchangeable with one: the whole value of naming it separately is the crossings the model then refuses.

### `ConnectorsCliConfig`

`loom.datasource.ConnectorsCliConfig` is a record of four fields:

- `program` — `String`
- `config` — `Optional<String>`, which may be absent
- `state_dir` — `Optional<String>`, which may be absent
- `timeout_seconds` — `Optional<Integer>`, which may be absent

### `DataSource`

`loom.datasource.DataSource` is a record of six fields:

- `name` — `loom.datasource.SourceName`
- `adapter` — `loom.datasource.AdapterAlias`
- `connection` — `loom.datasource.ConnectionId`
- `list` — `Optional<loom.datasource.OperationId>`, which may be absent
- `search` — `Optional<loom.datasource.OperationId>`, which may be absent
- `get` — `Optional<loom.datasource.OperationId>`, which may be absent

### `OperationId`

`loom.datasource.OperationId` wraps `String` and is not interchangeable with one: the whole value of naming it separately is the crossings the model then refuses.

### `ReadKind`

`loom.datasource.ReadKind` is one of `List`, `Search` and `Get`.

### `ReadRefusal`

`loom.datasource.ReadRefusal` is a record of five fields:

- `source` — `Optional<loom.datasource.SourceName>`, which may be absent
- `adapter` — `loom.datasource.AdapterAlias`
- `operation` — `Optional<loom.datasource.OperationId>`, which may be absent
- `code` — `String`
- `message` — `String`

### `ReadResult`

`loom.datasource.ReadResult` is a record of two fields:

- `body` — `Json`
- `audit_ref` — `Optional<String>`, which may be absent

### `SourceEntity`

`loom.datasource.SourceEntity` is a record of four fields:

- `operation` — `loom.datasource.OperationId`
- `schema` — `String`
- `input_schema` — `Json`
- `revision` — `String`

### `SourceName`

`loom.datasource.SourceName` wraps `String` and is not interchangeable with one: the whole value of naming it separately is the crossings the model then refuses.

Three of the types above are reached by nothing else in this system: `loom.datasource.ReadRefusal`, `loom.datasource.ReadResult` and `loom.datasource.SourceEntity`. No entity, view, command, event, error or crossing names them, so it is either vocabulary something outside this specification uses or a leftover — and only a person can tell which.
